blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 84 in June to 93 in September (+10.7%), and it took 9.1% of the city’s 351 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings fell from 40 in June to 37 in September (−7.5%), and it took 2.5% of the city’s 591 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Bear Creek Green Timbers for detached houses in June (a sellers’ best bet); detached houses in August (a buyers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: Lot fabric, as the research states it: an established central-Surrey sub-area whose live-page character copy describes larger lots and mature trees beside the two parks, with diverse housing from character homes to renovated properties and occasional new builds — that description is site copy, labelled as such, not a verified lot-size profile. The feed snapshot mixes detached houses (including suite-heavy detached listings, and one house lot marketed in its listing text to builders) with the 81a Avenue condo cluster and townhouse pockets. No typical lot size, lot count or lot price is stated — none is documented on an official source for this sub-area.
Fee-simple lots are the default form: A sub-area-wide strata-versus-freehold split is UNVERIFIED — no official source publishes one.

Bare-land strata — its own form, stated plainly: a bare-land strata lot IS strata tenure on the lot itself — Form B, strata fees for common property and registered bylaws apply to the lot; it is NOT fee-simple.

Park and creek ground sorts the diligence, not the marketing: No parcel-level riparian setback figure is documented in this research for any lot here — none is invented; the setback is read off the parcel's stream class in COSMOS and Part 7A before design work.
Named buildings/complexes — cross-reference ONLY, never land: None is a land development, a subdivision or a lot offering here.

Assemblies / development sites / rezoning proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented in this sub-area's research. The one documented change at the sub-area's edge is transit infrastructure — Green Timbers Station on the Surrey Langley SkyTrain (anticipated in-service 2029) — which is a project station, not a development site and not land inventory.

ALR vs non-ALR split: no ALR parcel in this sub-area is documented in this research and no split is published — none is stated. A specific parcel's reserve status is checked on the ALC maps by PID or civic address.
: No phase selling vacant lots is documented in this sub-area. Never mixed with built presales.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: Bear Creek Green Timbers is one board sub-area with a compound name — one of 15 sub-areas of the Fraser Valley board community "Surrey" in the SnapStats data — not two separate areas for "Bear Creek" and "Green Timbers." The live page is headed "Bear Creek Green Timbers Homes for Sale | Surrey Real Estate," and its feed showed 137 results ("1-12 / 137") at reading — a snapshot, not a market statistic. (as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report)
The feed's first-page cards span Surrey postal codes V3W, V3S, V3R and V3V, mixing detached houses, condo apartments and townhouses.

Municipal geography: the ground sits inside the City of Surrey. The City places Bear Creek Park in Whalley, beside the Surrey Arts Centre, while Green Timbers is the urban-forest ground in the city's north-centre; the City lists seven communities (City Centre, Cloverdale, Fleetwood, Guildford, Newton, South Surrey, Whalley) and "Bear Creek Green Timbers" is not one of them. A finer City planning breakdown of this exact sub-area ground: UNVERIFIED in the research pass (429 — stopped, not retried).

The two green spaces the name joins: Bear Creek Park (placed by the City in Whalley) and Green Timbers Urban Forest, whose westernmost edge will host the Green Timbers SkyTrain Station at 140 Street and Fraser Highway. Detail on either park from the City's own park pages (sizes, facilities, trail lengths): UNVERIFIED in the research pass (429).
Sub-area medians are not published (UNVERIFIED at sub-area level).

Schools (Ministry-listed names and addresses only, in and around this ground): Bear Creek Elementary, 13780 80 Ave; Green Timbers Elementary, 8824 144 St; Newton Elementary, 13359 81 Ave; Janice Churchill Elementary, 8226 146 St; Sullivan Elementary, 6016 152 St; Frank Hurt Secondary, 13940 77 Ave; Enver Creek Secondary, 14505 84 Ave; North Surrey Secondary, 15945 96 Ave; Kwantlen Park Secondary, 10441 132 St; Sullivan Heights Secondary, 6248 144 St; Fleetwood Park Secondary, 7940 156 St.

Transit edge: the Surrey Langley SkyTrain is a 16-kilometre Expo Line extension along Fraser Highway from King George Station to 203 Street in Langley City, with an anticipated in-service date of 2029; Green Timbers Station (140 Street and Fraser Highway) is its station at this sub-area's north edge. Current bus route detail for the sub-area: UNVERIFIED in the research pass.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect land buyers in Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: SSMUH / added units (Surrey framework, adopted Jul 8, 2024): a maximum of 3 units on lots smaller than 280 m², 4 units on lots larger than 280 m², and up to 6 units on eligible lots of at least 281 m² within 400 m of a frequent bus stop, on eligible residential lots under 4,050 m² within the Urban Containment Boundary. Added-unit permission is NOT permission to subdivide and does not create new lots.

Secondary suites (Bylaw No. 12000, as verified in the program's rules-gaps pass): one secondary suite may be permitted per single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit; a suite is not permitted within a coach house or garden suite; a suite's habitable floor area may not exceed 40% of the principal dwelling unit; no 90 m² cap was found in the current consolidated bylaw text; and a suite is not a separate strata lot.

Coach houses and garden suites (rules-gaps verified): all Surrey residential zones that allow detached houses, duplexes and houseplexes also allow a coach house or garden suite; the unit must be at least 35 m² and at most 75 m², rising to 120 m² for lots zoned RA, R2, R2-O and R3 where the existing house or duplex is below maximum FAR; smaller R3–R6 lots require lane access for a coach house; one extra parking space is required.

Streamside / riparian — the creek diligence item for this sub-area: Surrey's streamside setbacks are defined in Part 7A of Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, with different setbacks applied to various types of streams, complemented by the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit (SEDP) process — a parcel near Bear Creek or another watercourse is checked against its stream class in COSMOS and Part 7A, and no single setback figure is stated for the sub-area because the bylaw sets them by class.

ALR block (provincial frame — no sub-area ALR parcel is documented in the research, stated so it is not misapplied): subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s.6; SPA s.239; ALCA s.21(1)); caps: principal ≤500 m², suite within principal only, additional residence 90 m² (≤40 ha) / 186 m² (>40 ha). Farm class is three-tier — $2,500 on 0.8–4 ha / $2,500 + 5% of value over 4 ha / $10,000 under 0.8 ha, applications by Oct 31 — a flat "$2,500+" line is an ERROR, and no farm-class claim is asserted for this sub-area.

blocks.text: Good to know about Bear Creek Green Timbers

items.t: The board name and the City's map disagree, and both are right. "Bear Creek Green Timbers" exists only as a board sub-area; the City frames the same ground through Whalley, Newton, Fleetwood and Guildford, and places Bear Creek Park itself in Whalley beside the Surrey Arts Centre. A City plan search run under the board name finds nothing — search by parcel in COSMOS instead.

One name, two forms on the same avenue. The Trails name on 84 Avenue covers a townhouse component and an apartment building at different addresses (plus a directory address that could not be resolved to either in the townhomes pass) — a name-based search mixes them, and neither is land.
The "164-acre Bear Creek Park" figure is listing text, not a City figure.
Small counts make this sub-area's pace a signal, not a trend.

Suite income is the detached story here — and the permit is the diligence. The feed's detached listings lean on basement suites; Surrey's rule is one suite per unit at ≤40% of the principal unit with no suite inside a coach house — a listing's suite count is not proof of a permitted suite.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Bear Creek Green Timbers than in June?
faq.a: In Bear Creek Green Timbers, listings of houses rose from 84 in June to 93 in September (+10.7%); condos and townhomes fell from 40 in June to 37 in September (−7.5%).

faq.q: How big is Bear Creek Green Timbers compared with the rest of Surrey?
faq.a: In September 2026, Bear Creek Green Timbers held 8.3% of the 1,120 houses listed in Surrey and 2.4% of the 1,523 condos and townhomes listed in Surrey.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Bear Creek Green Timbers from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 32 houses and 15 condos and townhomes sold in Bear Creek Green Timbers over those 4 months.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Bear Creek Green Timbers?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Bear Creek Green Timbers?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Is Bear Creek Green Timbers one area or two?
faq.a: One board sub-area with a compound name — a single sub-area of the Surrey community in the SnapStats data, joining the Bear Creek Park ground (which the City places in Whalley) with the Green Timbers Urban Forest ground. It is not one of the City's seven community names.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot here?
faq.a: No named bare-land subdivision or lot offering was verified in this sub-area. What trades as land is the existing fabric — detached house lots, including suite-heavy houses and the occasional lot marketed to builders in listing text — each checked parcel by parcel in COSMOS.

faq.q: What creek or park diligence applies to a lot near Bear Creek Park?
faq.a: The streamside check: Surrey's setbacks sit in Part 7A of Bylaw No. 12000 and vary by stream class, with the Sensitive Ecosystems Development Permit process alongside — read the parcel's class and permit-area position in COSMOS before design work. No single setback figure is stated for the sub-area, because the bylaw does not set one.

faq.q: Can a house lot here add a suite or a coach house?
faq.a: One secondary suite per dwelling unit, capped at 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area and never inside a coach house or garden suite; a coach house or garden suite of 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR, with lane access required on smaller lots and one extra parking space). Verify a suite's permit status rather than relying on listing text.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a lot here, or build multiple units instead?
faq.a: Different permissions: SSMUH allows 3–4 units on most lots by size band (up to 6 near a frequent bus stop), but that does not create new lots; subdivision must meet the zone minimum in Bylaw No. 12000 and the servicing requirements under the Surrey Subdivision and Development Bylaw, 1986, No. 8830, confirmed with the City per parcel.
